en: You were shown to Leafa's room.{w}

"I simply adore shortbread made with the Sweet Ginger that grows in the Nerid Marshlands."{w}{p}"It's so sweet, with just a hint of spice. But thanks to how dangerous things have become lately, I can't send anyone out to fetch it."{w}{p}"...And so.{w}I would like you to go and gather some Sweet Ginger for me."{w}
Will you fetch it for me?
"........"{w}{p}"You are lowly adventurers.{w}I am royalty.{w}Surely you understand how you ought to answer?"{w}
note: Reply to choosing 'no'. Ou-kou-kizoku rendered 'royalty' (she is a princess).

en: "Hee hee. Thank you.{w}Well then, I'm counting on you."{w}
Swept along by Leafa, who would not take no for an answer, you left the room.{w}
You entered the castle, but then realized you hadn't brought any Sweet Ginger.{w}{p}Even if you forced your way in to see Leafa, you'd only be thrown out.{w}
You called on Leafa with the Sweet Ginger.{w}{p}Looking thoroughly put out, the guard showed you to Leafa's room.{w}
"I see. This is Sweet Ginger indeed."{w}
"Very well done~{w}Oh, I know! I shall make you my very own personal adventurers."{w}{p}"I hereby issue you this."{w}

"This is the gear issued to the Royal Knights.{w}Normally, adventurers like you would never get your hands on it in your whole lives."{w}{p}"It's proof that you have become my knights. Do take good care of it."{w}{p}"Now then, with that settled, shall I make my next request?"{w}{p}"My next request is the Moonlight Stone.{w}I would like you to take back the Moonlight Stone from the Old Man of the Moon, who appears at the top of Moonlight Falls."{w}{p}"The Moonlight Stone was originally one of the hidden treasures of the Isfald royal family.{w}It was a precious gift from my father."{w}{p}"It's a gem that grows brighter when it absorbs the light of a night rainbow. If you hold it up to the 'Midnight Rainbow' that forms where the water of the falls meets the moonlight,"{w}{p}"it keeps that brilliance for quite some time."{w}{p}"We use it for festivals and ceremonies, so we would send someone out regularly to hold it up to the Midnight Rainbow, but..."{w}{p}"the Old Man of the Moon was so bewitched by its beauty that he stole it."{w}{p}"We've sent soldiers a number of times, but it never seems to go well."{w}{p}"The Midnight Rainbow should be appearing again soon. Could you get the Moonlight Stone back from the Old Man of the Moon when he shows up?"{w}{p}"You are now officially my knights. From now on, just tell the guards whose service you're in, and you'll be able to come straight to my room."{w}
note: Bugu (arms/armour) = 'gear'. Tsuki no Okina = 'the Old Man of the Moon' (new term; glossary notes it is the Lunatic Demon's self-name, male). Mayonaka no Niji = 'Midnight Rainbow' (new term), single quotes where the source uses double brackets. Shozoku wo ieba = 'tell the guards whose service you're in'. The row break after 'moonlight,' mirrors the source, which cuts the sentence across two pages.

en: "Now, go forth! From this day on, you are my very own order of knights, the 'Sweet Ginger Knights'!"{w}
You entered the castle, but then realized you hadn't brought the Moonlight Stone.{w}{p}Even if you forced your way in to see Leafa, you'd only be thrown out.{w}
When you told the guards whose service you were in, you were shown to Leafa's room.{w}
"Why, this is the Moonlight Stone indeed!{w}Ahh, what a ridiculously beautiful glow...{w}You've done well."{w}
note: Muda ni utsukushii ('wastefully beautiful') = 'ridiculously beautiful', keeping the comic over-the-top note.

en: "This is your reward."{w}
"Also, if you'd like... have some of this.{w}I made it with the Sweet Ginger from the other day."{w}
You were offered shortbread along with black tea.{w}You popped one into your mouth. It tasted dry and stodgy.{w}

Like chewing sand. For some reason, those words came to mind.{w}A sandstorm raged in your mouth. You needed something to drink, right now.{w}{p}You quickly took a sip of tea, but the moisture you'd hoped for was swallowed up by the sandstorm.{w}Actually, no -- the sand soaked up the tea and turned into a gel.{w}{p}It made no sense whatsoever.{w}{p}As you reached for the tea again, chewing and wondering what to do, you noticed Leafa watching your reaction with great interest.{w}{p}She must have made them herself.{w}Which means what awaits you next is the toughest question of the century...{w}
note: Source writes sosyaku (lend/lease) for soshaku (chew); a typo, rendered as chewing. 'Suna wo kamu' kept as the literal image. The casual 'tte iu ka' aside = 'Actually, no --'.

en: How is it? ...I-is it delicious?
note: Choice prompt; kept short.

en: "Really!?{w}Th-there's more, you know! As a special favor, I'll let you take it all home!!"{w}
"I'm so glad you like i..."{w}
note: Deliberately cut off mid-word, as in the source (she catches herself).

en: "!!"{w}{p}"O-of course it's delicious, I made it myself!!{w}Honestly, what a foolish question..."{w}
note: She calls her own question foolish; kept as the source has it (comic flustered reversal).

en: "People who are slow to learn are such a bother..."{w}{p}"You are lowly adventurers.{w}I am royalty.{w}Surely you understand how you ought to answer?"{w}
note: Reply to 'no'; repeats 4414 wording deliberately (same Japanese).

en: How is it? Delicious?
note: Choice prompt, repeated without the stammer.

en: "Yes, yes, honesty is the best policy~"{w}

"Now, that's enough of our pleasant teatime.{w}Next, I would like you to bring me the Holy Ember from the top floor of the Scorching Castle."{w}{p}"The Holy Ember is also an ember that never goes out."{w}{p}"Wouldn't it be lovely to make it into a lamp and carry it with me always?"{w}{p}"And so... I'm counting on you for the Holy Ember."{w}{p}"Now, go forth, 'Sweet Ginger Knights'!!"{w}
note: Seinaru Hidane = 'Holy Ember' (new item name, not in the glossary; ITEM.CSV:259 slot max 20 chars).

en: You entered the castle, but then realized you hadn't brought the Holy Ember.{w}{p}Even if you forced your way in to see Leafa, you'd only be thrown out.{w}
"You've obtained the Holy Ember!"{w}
"Your work is rather good.{w}Just what I'd expect from adventurers I picked out myself."{w}{p}"As a special favor, I shall arrange for you to buy the knights' armor as you please."{w}
Starting with your next visit to the castle, you can buy Elven Chain and Elven Chain +1 freely.{w}

"At night, once my official duties are done, I've been writing my personal history."{w}{p}"Well, it's something like a diary. I'm sure that with this light, I'll be able to write at my leisure."{w}{p}"And so... writing only about my own glorious achievements wouldn't be bad either, but..."{w}{p}"S-since you are my personal order of knights, I thought I'd do you the special honor of including your names."{w}
note: Jibunshi = 'personal history' (her memoir-diary).

en: "So... um... would you tell me your full names?"{w}{p}"I just remembered.{w}I never properly asked your names..."{w}
Tell her your full names?
"Really?{w}You'll tell me!?{w}Thank y..."{w}
note: Cut off mid-word, as in the source.

en: "!!"{w}{p}"N-naturally you would!{w}I won't permit you to refuse my offer, you hear!?"{w}{p}"Honestly, don't get carried away! This is why adventurers are so... grumble, grumble..."{w}
Leafa asked each of you your name in turn and diligently wrote them all down in her diary.{w}
"What? You won't?"{w}
"........"{w}{p}"...Well, I suppose you have your reasons. I won't force you."{w}
"I'll just put you down as 'A' or 'Mx. X' or something!"{w}
note: Source: 'A'-san (hiragana a) or 'A'-san (Latin A), i.e. first-letter placeholder names. The kana/Latin pair cannot carry over; rendered as two placeholder names, gender-neutral.

en: "Now I can make my personal history all the richer.{w}Hee hee...~"{w}{p}"Now then, there's still some time left today. I shall tell you an old tale handed down in the elven royal family."{w}{p}"Only fragments of it remain, though..."{w}

Long ago, all of us -- elves, ogres, humans, every race alike -- were on the brink of a great destruction.{w}{p}Our meager strength could not resist it, but it's said there was someone who saved us from that destruction.{w}{p}That person, with no thought for themselves, carved out a tomorrow for us.{w}{p}But the passing of time is an ungrateful thing.{w}In this age, not even that person's name has come down to us.{w}All that has come down to us is...{w}{p}an ancient promise: that when the time came, we elves would call out across the whole continent, seek that person out, and celebrate our reunion. In other words, Oldaim.{w}{p}For the reunion, it's said the 'Yuan Wine' that the ogres have long guarded is needed as a celebratory gift.{w}{p}Father and the ministers don't seem to sense anything, but I feel that now, of all times, we must act.{w}{p}Perhaps it even has something to do with the strange upheaval happening to the land right now.{w}
note: Leafa's story, unquoted in the source; her voice kept. 'Sono kata' (the savior, in fact Urna) left as 'that person / themselves' because the tale deliberately hides who it is. 'Oldaim' (the castle name, glossary) is the name of the promise; the English 'Old Aim' reading comes for free, so no gloss added.

en: "Actually, the next thing I'd like you to do is look into this legend.{w}I shall issue you a royal command."{w}{p}"With a royal command from the elven royal family, the ogres should share some of their Yuan Wine with you."{w}{p}"Take it, and find the one who saved our lives, who must be somewhere in this land. Would you do that?"{w}{p}"Right now, everyone is in an uproar over the whole business at Contrachio.{w}You're the only ones I can as..."{w}
note: Cut off before 'ask' (tanome...); the next row shows she stops herself from asking a favor.

en: "Ugh! Why should I have to bow my head to mere adventurers!?{w}That's an order! Go!!"{w}
note: Dakara! = exasperated self-interruption, 'Ugh!'.

en: "........{w}This journey may be more dangerous than any so far."{w}{p}"Do be careful out there.{w}You mustn't push yourselves too hard, all right?"{w}
"You are my knights now. It's your duty to come back safe and sound, understand!?"{w}
"Now go forth, 'Sweet Ginger Knights'!!"{w}
"Have you obtained the 'Yuan Wine'?{w}Go and ask the king of the ogres and goblins at Baroque Fort."{w}
note: 'Oga ya goburin no ou' read as 'the kings of the ogres and goblins'; the ogre ruler is a queen (glossary) and the goblin ruler King Montana, so 'rulers'. Could also parse as 'the ogres, or the goblin king'. Accuracy: one king, not 'rulers'. Montana (male, King of Baroque Fort) hands over the wine and says 'we ogres and goblins' (slice 049, SCD11:2807); the ogre queen Domanaya belongs to the ancient recording.

en: "So they let you have it! Well done!{w}Now all that's left is to find the one we should give this wine to...{w}What should we do, I wonder?"{w}
"If only I had some idea..."{w}
"You've found the one who saved us, you say?{w}...What!? Urna...???"{w}
"You're telling me the evil spirit that appeared at Contrachio is the one!?"{w}
You told her everything that led you to Urna.{w}
"No...{w}We banished the very one who saved our lives... Ahh...!!"{w}
Leafa lowered her eyes sadly.{w}
"So Queen Ragnastia of Bistel knew all along, and still ordered Lady Urna struck down."{w}
note: Urna-sama = 'Lady Urna' (Urna is female per glossary).

en: "Even if it was to keep everyone's way of life going...{w}carrying that burden all alone must have been so painful for her."{w}{p}"So that's how it was..."{w}
note: 'Her' = Queen Ragnastia (honorific o-tsurakatta, female per glossary).

en: "How shameful we are.{w}Unwilling to give up the lives we have now, we broke our promise and banished the savior whose return we were meant to celebrate..."{w}{p}"What I can forgive least of all is that, even knowing all this, some part of me is relieved!!"{w}
"I am... the very worst...!{w}Ngh..."{w}
Gone was her usual haughty air; tears streamed endlessly from Leafa's eyes.{w}To comfort her, you passed on Urna's words.{w}
"...Lady Urna says she forgives us?{w}Us, who repaid her kindness with betrayal!?{w}How can she be so... so warm-hearted..."{w}
"I shall never forget Lady Urna as long as I live."{w}
"I may not be able to make it public, but I shall engrave it deep in my heart: that there was someone who poured great love upon us."{w}
"Today's diary entry will surely take me until dawn."{w}{p}"You have done well, all of you.{w}I thank you from the bottom of my heart."{w}

"So you've come!"{w}{p}"I'm cooped up in the castle all the time, so I'm bored to tears."{w}{p}"Anything at all will do. Won't you tell me some fun story from your travels?{w}I'll have tea and sweets brought in!"{w}
note: Repeat-visit greeting after the quest line.

en: Elven Chain costs {0B:0001:1A90} GP.{w}
Elven Chain +1 costs {0B:0001:4690} GP.{w}
What will you do?
Seek an audience with Leafa
Back
Buy Elven Chain
note: Source abbreviates to 'Elven'; full item name fits.

en: Buy Elven Chain +1
Armitt
note: Glossary: Armitt (washerwoman, Gregorio's mother). Not Almite (arumaito), the wiped-out adventurer.

en: "Would you look at that!{w}Perfect weather for doing the laundry!"{w}{p}"Are you lot adventurers?{w}Well, you make a living at it, so good on you."{w}
note: Accuracy: verb restored (BASE_RULES pro-drop rule).

en: "I've got an only son myself, name of Gregorio, but..."{w}{p}"He's forever sponging off his parents. He's hopeless, I tell you!"{w}{p}"I wish he'd hurry up and stand on his own two feet."{w}

"Once the laundry's done, I've got the shopping to do...{w}Just look at these arms!"{w}{p}"Before I married, I'm sure I was a dainty, pretty young thing who looked lovely in lace gloves."{w}{p}"Now I'm a middle-aged frump who looks right at home with a ratty oven mitt...{w}...Heave-ho!"{w}
note: Yokkorasho = effort grunt as she lifts something (laundry).

en: "By the way, that's my son Gregorio over there. Here he comes again with that idiot face of his.{w}I bet he's after more pocket money again..."{w}
note: Accuracy: subject restored (BASE_RULES pro-drop rule).

en: "BLEHHHHH!{w}Hey, you old hag! Hand over my allowance, dammit!!"{w}
note: Speaker ??? (Gregorio before his name box). Bero-on = tongue-wagging sound (rocker pose; he wears makeup, next slice). Insult kept at full force.

en: "Gregorio! What kind of way is that to talk to your own mother!?"{w}
